original_question: Let K_0, K_1, K_2, K_3, S, M, and G be the classes of groups considered in the paper, and recall that Theorem 1.1 proves the following statement whenever A and B are members of this collection with B properly contained in A and A containing K_3: there is no algorithm that decides, given a finite presentation of a group known to lie in A, whether that group lies in B. Does the same undecidability statement remain true in the case A = K_2?
target_in_paper: Section 1, immediately after Theorem 1.1: the unnumbered conjectural extension of Theorem 1.1 to the case A = K_2.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the paper’s main undecidability theorem, uses the right family of classes, keeps the input model as finite group presentations, and focuses on exactly the excluded case singled out in the introduction: whether the Theorem 1.1 recognition-undecidability statement should still hold when A = K_2.
missing_details: In the paper this is not stated as a separate numbered conjecture; the nearest official formulation is the unnumbered sentence immediately following Theorem 1.1 in the introduction.
Once A = K_2, the only proper subclasses B from the paper’s list are K_0 and K_1; the draft leaves this quantifier implicit.
K_n is defined in Section 2 as the class of groups of complements of locally flat PL embeddings S^n into S^{n+2}; thus K_2 means 2-knot groups in that PL, locally flat sense.

The paper formalizes this as a recognition problem on finite presentations; its well-posedness uses the recursive enumerability of the relevant presentation sets, proved for K_0, K_1, and K_2 in Theorem 2.8.
The paper gives a conditional partial result that your draft omits: the conjectured extension to A = K_2 is said to hold provided there exists a group in K_2 with unsolvable word problem.

The closely related end-of-paper question 'Is there a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem?' is supporting context, but it is not itself the same question as the conjectural extension of Theorem 1.1.
refined_question: Let K_n denote the class of fundamental groups of complements of locally flat PL embeddings S^n into S^{n+2}. Theorem 1.1 proves that if A and B are chosen from {K_0, K_1, K_2, K_3, S, M, G} with B properly contained in A and A containing K_3, then there is no algorithm which, given a finite presentation of a group known a priori to lie in A, decides whether that group lies in B. Does this same undecidability statement remain true when A = K_2; equivalently, for each B in {K_0, K_1}, is there no algorithm that, given a finite presentation of a group known to be a 2-knot group, decides whether the presented group lies in B? The paper notes that this would follow if some 2-knot group has unsolvable word problem.
justification: The draft is already aimed at the correct place in the paper, but the paper’s exact target is slightly sharper and narrower. The relevant statement is not a broader neighboring open problem, but the introduction’s unnumbered conjecture that Theorem 1.1 should also hold for K_2. To make the question stand alone and paper-faithful, one must unpack that with A = K_2 only B = K_0 or B = K_1 are relevant, specify that K_2 means 2-knot groups arising from locally flat PL 2-spheres in S^4, and record the paper’s stated conditional evidence: this extension would follow if there exists a 2-knot group with unsolvable word problem. The end-of-paper question about existence of such a group is related context, but it is not the same conjecture.
